column1: # The 10 qiraat, the reciters who transmit them, and the 20 riwayahs.
# WHY THIS IS A REGISTRY AND NOT 49 DICTIONARY ENTRIES
# The dictionary defines concepts: what a `qiraah` is, what a `riwayah` is,
# what a `rawi` is. Those three entries answer "what is this?". Hafs is not
# another concept — he is a member of a set the concept already defines. A
# closed set of members belongs in a registry, the way the twenty-eight letter
# Every other name in this standard is derived from vocalized Arabic by
# tools/translit.py, because a term is a word with a meaning and the derivation
# keeps it. These are people. A person's name carries no meaning to keep, so
# deriving it invents a spelling nobody writes and gains nothing. The name is
# written the way it is commonly written, and the `alternative_spellings`
# column carries the other attested forms so all of them resolve to one member.
# This is the same exception, for the same reason, as letter names.
# "Commonly written" still needs an authority, or it is taste wearing a
# different hat. `transliteration` is the scholarly English form as English
# scholarship on the qiraat writes it, with its diacritics; `display` is that
# form with the diacritics and the hamzah and ayn marks removed, which is what
# English prose and code actually carry. So the display name is derived after
# all — from the English rendering rather than from the Arabic. Where the two
# would disagree over a ta marbutah the standard's own rule wins: Shubah, not
# Shuba, because section 5 governs the ending and the source only spells it.
# `<rawi>_an_<qiraah>` — hafs_an_asim, warsh_an_nafi. The form is not optional:
# it is what disambiguates al-Duri, who transmits from two imams, and Khalaf,
# who is a rawi of Hamzah and an imam in his own right. Short forms that happen
# to be unambiguous (ishaq_an_khalaf) are listed as alternative spellings, not
# A QIRAAH IS NAMED BY ITS IMAM
# `asim` is the qiraah of Asim, and the same string identifies the imam. This
# follows use; it is not a claim that a reading and a person are one thing.
# `numbering` is the ayah-numbering system conventionally paired with the
# qiraah. It is a property of the counting school, not of the reading, and the
# two are paired by convention — see standards/terminology/concepts/
# ayah_numbering_system.yml. It is recorded here because software that stores a
# NOT ENUMERATED HERE: the turuq, and here is exactly why.
# Al-Nashr names the routes below each riwayah, and at the level of tariq the
# 10 readings run to some 980 of them. Reading them out of the isnad section
# was tried: a scan of its hundred pages yields 416 occurrences of "tariq X"
# resolving to 224 distinct names. They are chain links at every depth of the
# tree, and prose gives no reliable way to attach each one to its parent.
# Worse, there is no way to check the result — the ayah counts could be proved
# right because they reconcile to totals the book itself states, and the turuq
# have no such total to reconcile against. An unverifiable 40-row table would
# look exactly like a verified one, which is the argument against writing it.
# The route level applications actually store — «من طريق الشاطبية», «طيبة النشر»,
# al-Durrah, al-Taysir — is in registries/tariq.tsv: each is a book whose name has
# become the name of the path below the rawi that it fixes, which is the sense
# To close this: work from al-Nashr's per-riwayah sections rather than a regex,
# and find a count the result must reconcile to before trusting any of it.
# `ref` cites al-Nashr fi al-Qiraat al-Ashr, ed. al-Dabba, as volume/page — the
# page of the isnad section that names the imam together with both of his ruwat.
